focus.name: 9mm SIG P365, concealed-carry
focus.description: Bought two months before Ep 1 after being jumped and mugged near his warehouse; he got the CCP through the warehouse's security-role paperwork afterwards, and it's still fresh enough that he re-reads the permit conditions when he's nervous. **The permit issued about six months before Ep 5** — recent enough that anyone who runs his ID can see it is new. In-domain: whatever's coming at the people behind you goes somewhere else. You step between; it finds another target, loses interest, or turns out not to have been aimed at them. It works holstered.
focus.inFlightVariant: Mars could not carry the pistol on an international flight to Taiwan (Taiwanese law is severe). In Ep 1 he carried the magazine-shaped keychain (a deactivated novelty gun part; see focusNotes) — a muscle-memory anchor for the weapon he wasn't wearing. Same domain, same focus by cognitive-anchor logic; the object he touches when he needs to feel his own shape in a room. Since returning home (Ep 2 onward), he carries the pistol again.
focus.rangeHabit: He went to the range four or five times in the first weeks, seriously, with the focus of someone doing homework. He has been maybe twice since. **The pistol is an anchor, not a skill** — the object he touches to feel his own shape in a room — and he is quietly aware that he is not especially good with it. He does not volunteer this. If a scene asks whether he trains, this is the answer unless his player says otherwise; do NOT drift him toward competence, because his Phase-2 release moment is standing his ground WITHOUT it.

meaningfulItem: 9mm SIG P365, concealed-carry — bought two months before Ep 1 after being jumped near the warehouse. In-flight variant: a magazine-shaped keychain when he can't carry.
specificPlace: The abandoned grain silos on the Pier 80 side of the port — he knows every catwalk by memory.
intentionUnderPressure: My mother lived in that Dogpatch apartment thirty years. She was priced out last year. The paperwork was clean, the notice was legal, and I couldn't stop it. Afterward I started organizing on the side, because the next old woman on the block isn't going to lose her place because nobody was standing there when the notice came.
backstory:
Mars grew up in Dogpatch and has watched every wave of development eat the neighborhood he learned to walk in. He enrolled at SF State's business school at 18, dropped out at 20 when the money got tight, took a warehouse job that was supposed to be temporary, and has been there five years. He runs the shift now. He started organizing on the side after his mother was priced out of her apartment of thirty years last year.

Two months before Ep 1, he was jumped outside the Pier 80 gate at 4am end-of-shift. Two men, one hit, one grabbed the wallet. He was on the ground for a minute before he could stand up. He was fine. He wasn't fine. He bought the pistol the following week and got the permit through work.

He met Morgan on a War Thunder forum eight months ago; they became close friends over long late-night voice calls where Morgan doesn't talk about 'the industry' and Mars doesn't talk about the mugging. The Taipei trip was Morgan's idea and Mars's excuse — he was burnt out, wanted to disappear for a couple weeks, and Morgan was going anyway.

Height has been the single most consistent fact of his social life since sixth grade. He does not talk about it. If you bring it up, he will out-argue you and remember.

bonds.name: Morgan Reyes
bonds.description: The War Thunder friend, Taipei co-conspirator. Closer than either says.

bonds: **Alaia Vega** — the Bodie ranger. She remembered him making cocoa at the Union Hall, and when Dakota's antics stalled at Caffè Strada she spent a long stretch talking with Mars instead. Two people who are responsible for others at work.

dmNotes.want: **Be standing there when it happens.** Not winning and not stopping it — he could not stop it and knows he could not. The paperwork was clean and the notice was legal. **The want is presence at the moment of the refusal**, which is why it survives losing.
dmNotes.wantForgedAgainst: Against a refusal: *"The paperwork was clean, the notice was legal, and I couldn't stop it."*
dmNotes.wantArticulationBeat: **Ep 6, the dance floor** — he is asked to dance and cannot decline gracefully. **Not an official refusing him — the room OFFERING him something he has no standing to accept or refuse.** His want is *be standing there when it happens*; here presence is the whole ask, and it costs him.
dmNotes.wantSealNote: **SEALED — never shown to the player. Played behaviour beats it.** See `wants-sealed.md`.
dmNotes.magicPhase: Realized (Ep 7, the piñata; ruled). Ep 8 names his ability to him plainly (ruled 2026-09-27; canonical in facts-ledger §50). Release (moment of release) still ahead.
dmNotes.intentionUnderPressureNote: **Note 2026-09-27:** the sheet's intention text below the fold was written DM-side, not by the player. The player's own chargen answers (private, outside the repo) are about protection — being picked on for his height, then mugged — and about fairness: the world favours the well-off, and people should be equal. **His domain (posture / protection) is grounded in those words.** The Dogpatch eviction remains his fictional backstory. The mugging is the cost signature (neck flare). Phase-2 release candidate: a scene where he stands between with the pistol NOT on him, and trouble goes elsewhere anyway — proof the protection is his, not the weapon's.
dmNotes.castDomain:
posture / protection (ruled 2026-09-27; canonical in facts-ledger §50) — **whatever is coming at the people behind him goes somewhere else**: a dog swerves toward a gull, a drunk loses the thread and gets off the bus, a scooter clips a crate instead, a tailing car loses interest. **Trigger: he physically steps between** ("I stand in front of [them]"). **The focus works holstered; drawing the pistol counts as aiming** (one tier worse) — the strength is in not needing it. **Works on** a person, animal or object with a direction. **Not** on institutions: once the ticket is filed or the notice served, it is out of his reach. **Boundary with {{pc:2}}:** *something coming at someone* is his; *a body in trouble* is hers. **Persuasion is never his magic** — talking someone round is a CHA / Influence roll. Magic is what charm cannot explain. Cost: bad sleep and the next-day neck flare from the mugging (see costTellPolicy).

**Played record under this domain:** Ep 2's tailing car that lost interest is his FIRST cast (DM ruling 2026-09-27). **Ep 4's door at Vivian's was a successful CHA roll, not a cast** (retconned 2026-09-27). The Ep 7 piñata stays texture — his realization is ruled fired there, but Nia does not cite it as a cast.
dmNotes.costTellPolicy: The neck-flare (mugging-at-Pier-80 cost signature) fires prominently on FIRST cast and on Costly-tier or higher casts. For Cheap/Free-tier casts, log privately; mention on-page at DM's discretion, roughly 1 in 3. Overuse tedious; underuse loses the pattern. *(2026-09-27: the Ep 4 flare was delivered with a mundane reason — "you slept badly" — and stays harmless now that Elena's door is a CHA roll.)*
dmNotes.bringAGunWatch: Mars may want to bring the pistol into scenes where it doesn't help. Give him graceful ways to *not*. Some venues (state parks, government offices) will notice a concealed carry — a real logistical friction, not a moral one.
dmNotes.alignmentDriftWatch: Could drift toward Chaotic Good the more he protects the party. Could drift toward Neutral Evil if the mugging trauma routes into a revenge fixation.
dmNotes.focusNotes: If the pistol is confiscated in-scene, Mars needs to find a stand-in fast — the magazine-shaped keychain is still the fallback, per Ep 1 mechanic. **What it is (DM ruling 2026-09-27):** a deactivated, entirely harmless novelty gun part, magazine-shaped, legal everywhere — it gets eye-rolls in some countries and trouble in none. Earlier notes called it a holster clip; the object was never pinned down until Ep 7, where the kids took it, played hacky sack with it, and named him "Mezzanine".
dmNotes.playerStateSept2026:
**WHAT THE PLAYER HAS WORKED OUT, told to the DM directly (2026-09-06). This is the most useful thing anyone has handed us about {{pc:5}} and it changes how A7 should be run.**

- **He knows his domain is charisma / presence.** That part is settled for him. *(2026-09-27: probably read off his sheet, which printed "posture / presence" from Ep 3. Retconned to **posture / protection** — Ep 8's Nia tells him plainly; "charisma" becomes a CHA roll, never magic. See facts-ledger §50.)*
- **He does not know how to make it fire**, because so much of it is ordinary charisma and he cannot tell the two apart.
- **He believes that if he pushes too hard it will not work.**
- **He vaguely recalls it working at least once**, in a way that went beyond normal charisma.

> **HE IS RIGHT ABOUT THE RULE, AND HE DERIVED IT HIMSELF.** *Push too hard and it fails* is the **trying-too-hard tax** — an actual mechanic in `world/rules.md` that nobody has told him. **This is the second time a player has reverse-engineered a system rule from play** (the first was {{pc:4}}'s player arriving at `personaDropCanon` independently). **Do not confirm it and do not correct it. Let him keep being right.**

> ~~THE ONE HE HALF-REMEMBERS IS REAL AND IT IS ON THE RECORD: the presence-domain door-cast at Vivian's, Ep 4.~~ **RETCONNED 2026-09-27:** the door at Vivian's was a **successful CHA roll**, not a cast. His first cast is **Ep 2's tailing car** (DM ruling). What he half-remembers may be either; do not correct him — Ep 8 names the domain plainly and he can re-sort his own memories.

> **SO A7's REALIZATION IS NOT *did I cast* — IT IS *find the one charisma cannot explain*.** That reframes the beat entirely and makes it cheap: **he needs a case where charm was ruled out** — a room where he was not performing, or a result no amount of presence could have produced. **The problem he described to the DM IS the beat.** Do not solve it for him; build the room and let him rule charisma out.

> **THE ROOM IS EP 7 (ruled 2026-09-24):** at Mei's birthday he holds the piñata rope and says nothing, and the littlest ones keep coming back to lean on him. Four-year-olds are the audience charm cannot explain. Delivered by private slip; see the Ep 7 outline.
